Prompt entry kinds are system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument, toolResult and fragment.
Argument entries describe one MCP tool property and carry Parent tool and Field.
InputSchema[T] sets each tool property's description from its argument entry.
A mismatch between tool property and argument entry panics at server build.
jsonschema tags are not used for tool property descriptions.
Prompt templates use text/template, one set per resolve, with only the funcs inc and join.
An entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
Fragment entries are included via {{template}}.
Default prompts render byte-identical to the pre-P271 output, checked against testdata/golden.
RenderParts wraps each string variable in marker runes and splits, so Settings Preview can mark resolved values with VarText.

Prompt overrides are stored per app in <home>/llm-prompts.json, under ~/.kira-studio/ and ~/.kira-space/.
The llm-prompts.json file is written with renameio at mode 0600.

Saving a prompt's default text removes its override.
Override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash, and a stale change is refused with E_CONFLICT.
If the prompt store file is corrupt or an override no longer validates, the default is used and a warning is logged.
Corrupt or invalid prompt state is flagged in Settings with storeError and invalid.
defaultChanged flags an override made against an older default.
Server-side prompt validation requires the template to parse and every prompt:"required" variable to be referenced.
Server-side prompt validation requires every required fragment to be included and execution against example vars to succeed.
Memory system prompts must include memory.dataHygiene for injection defence.

dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild their MCP servers when the source Revision() changes.

checkprompts fails on jsonschema tags, and on MCP Tool, Prompt or PromptArgument Description or ServerOptions Instructions not from llmprompts.
checkprompts fails on memory.Call System not from llmprompts.
